transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-01
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Liam, Priya, Esther (Redwood) — Marcus, Aisha, Jamal, Sana (Solaris Insights)
Links shared: onboarding runbook https://redwood.ai/onboard-runbook, security docs link (SEC-POST)
---
[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Okay great, hi everyone, thanks for carving time. quick round-robin? i'll kick off — liam ortega from redwood, i'm the account exec on this.
[00:18] Marcus (Solaris): Marcus here — head of ML at Solaris. excited to kick this off, we got green light from execs last week.
[00:27] Aisha (Platform): Aisha, platform eng. we'll own infra and network. one thing up front: we need VPC peering or private link options.
[00:39] Jamal (Security): Jamal, security lead. SOC2 and KMS integration are must-haves, and we have to document audit trail for our compliance team.
[00:50] Esther (CSM): hey all — esther kim, your onboarding CSM. i'll own the runbook and success cadence. we'll propose a weekly 30-min sync during ramp.
[01:05] Priya (SE): priya shah, se. i'll run the technical deep dives — focusing on latency, kv cache, batching and dedicated capacity sizing.
[01:20] Sana (Product): sana — product. we'll integrate the api into our conversational ops product and need stable latencies under 150ms p50 for short prompts.
[02:00] Liam: thanks. goal today: align on success criteria, map stakeholders, confirm network/security constraints, and agree on next steps and owners.
[03:15] Marcus: quick context — pilots used open-source models in-house, but we spike on cost and ops maintenance. we want redwood to handle serving, but may need private deployment for regs.
[04:02] Priya: got it. can you share current traffic patterns? e.g., peak rps, avg tokens per request, and retention for kv cache.
[04:19] Marcus: peak 120 rps per region, avg 45 tokens, but some rerank workloads push to 800 tokens. we are ok with batching if latency impact is small.
[05:10] Aisha: and we want to avoid egress to public internet for PII flows — so VPC and customer-managed KMS.
[05:40] Jamal: also SSO via SAML is required for developer access, and role-based access for non-prod vs prod.
[06:02] Priya: perfect, that maps to Redwood Private options. for quick wins, hosted API for dev/proof-of-concept then dedicated pool or private deployment for prod — common pattern.
[06:22] Liam: can you walk me through the must-have success criteria so we can call it out in the runbook?
[06:38] Sana: p50 latency <150ms for short prompts, cost per 1k tokens < $X (will share target), throughput 100+ rps sustained per region, encryption at rest/in-transit, and audit logs for all model ops.
[07:12] Liam: noted. we'll add those to the success metrics section.
[07:30] Priya: quick note on latency: the combination of model variant (quantized vs high-precision) and batching affects p50. for your short prompts we'll recommend an LLM variant optimized for latency with small batch windows and pre-warmed kv cache.
[07:58] Marcus: what about rerank and longer sequences — you mentioned kernel selection earlier in the deck — how does that work?
[08:20] Priya: runtime will pick kernels based on sequence length distribution; for 800 token reranks we recommend a different instance type or dedicated lane. we can map traffic by route so rerank calls hit a high-memory pool and chat hits low-latency pool.
[08:45] Aisha: sounds sensible. can you do multi-pool routing? we may want fallbacks if dedicated nodes are at capacity.
[09:02] Esther: yes, we can configure smart routing and fallback to hosted or another variant, the runbook will include fallback policies and canary rollout steps.
[09:28] Jamal: on encryption and KMS — do you support customer-managed keys with HSM? we need to show that to auditors.
[09:45] Priya: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; hosted supports bring-your-own-KMS in certain regions — we'll validate with security docs.
[10:10] Liam: i'll flag that on the security checklist. esther will share SOC2 artifacts and the KMS integration guide after this call.
[10:22] Marcus: perfect. timeline — we're looking to start pilot in mid-august and prod by october. is that reasonable?
[10:36] Liam: yes — typical runway: week 0 onboarding and networking, week 1 performance tests, weeks 2–4 pilot ramp, then prod readiness. we'll align exact dates in a project plan.
[11:02] Priya: for the performance tests we'll need a sample prompt set and a traffic script — marcus, can your team own providing those?
[11:20] Marcus: yes, we'll deliver sample prompts and golden transcripts — target date 2026-08-05.
[11:40] Esther: action item noted: marcus provide prompt set (Aug 5).
[12:00] Aisha: on networking: we prefer VPC peering but are open to private link. which is faster to set up?
[12:18] Priya: usually private link is quicker with our hosted API; VPC peering is required for on-prem/private deployments and needs infra ticketing from both sides. we'll send network checklist.
[12:36] Jamal: and IP allowlist? we want to avoid opening broad ranges.
[12:48] Priya: we support IP allowlists and also mutual TLS for sensitive routes. details in the runbook network appendix.
[13:10] Liam: let's cover roles and access: who will need admin vs developer vs observer roles?
[13:24] Sana: devs need developer tokens for integration, platform eng needs admin, security gets observer + audit access.
[13:38] Esther: we'll send a template access matrix.
[14:05] Marcus: curious about observability — you mentioned token-level cost and latency breakdowns. how granular are those dashboards?
[14:26] Priya: per-route and per-model breakdown, token counts, p50/p95 latencies, and tracing that ties to prompts. we can also export to your datadog on a webhook.
[14:48] Aisha: good — send sample dashboard screenshots.
[15:06] Liam: i'll include links.
[15:30] Marcus: quick question — what about model version pinning and rollbacks? we need deterministic behavior for production.
[15:44] Priya: you can pin model versions per route, and we support canary rollouts + automatic fallback to previous versions if quality/regression alerts trigger.
[16:10] Jamal: do you store prompts for evals? any PII retention risk?
[16:24] Priya: by default we store telemetry; retention and redaction are configurable. for PII we recommend redaction on the client side and configuring no-persistence policies. we'll document options.
[16:48] Marcus: can we run a cost comparison for dedicated pool vs hosted with estimated token volumes?
[17:00] Liam: yes — we'll prepare a cost model spreadsheet showing break-even points by monthly tokens and expected savings with batching and quantization.
[17:20] Sana: for the pilot we want a small dedicated pool if it lowers variance, but not too expensive.
[17:36] Priya: we usually recommend a minimal dedicated pool for baseline throughput and then autoscale/burst to hosted if needed.
[18:02] Marcus: okay. one more — SSO. we use Okta, want SAML with SCIM for group sync.
[18:18] Esther: got it — we'll share SAML/SCIM checklist and coordinate with your IdP team.
[18:40] Aisha: what's the engineer on-call model for incidents during pilot?
[18:52] Liam: Redwood provides standard support for self-serve; for Dedicated/Private plans we provide a named CSE and 24/7 incident path depending on SLA. we'll include support contacts in the runbook.
[19:10] Marcus: good.
[19:30] Priya: technical deep dive proposal: week of Aug 10 — cover VPC setup, KMS exchange, sample perf test, and routing config.
[19:44] Marcus: that works. prefer Aug 11 afternoon.
[19:56] Esther: i'll send calendar invites after this call.
[20:10] Liam: recap — esther shares runbook, sso and security docs; priya preps vpc diagram + perf test plan; marcus provides sample prompts and RPS; jamal confirms kms vendor; i'll send pricing and project timeline.
[20:40] Marcus: sounds good. any blockers we should flag now?
[20:52] Jamal: need to validate KMS vendor compatibility — that's the critical path.
[21:05] Priya: we'll prioritize that in the deep dive and run a quick compatibility check.
[21:20] Sana: do you need access to our staging env or will you spin up test stubs?
[21:32] Priya: we'll do both — synthetic traffic from our test harness and optionally run in your staging with VPC peering.
[21:50] Aisha: ok we'll coordinate infra access.
[22:10] Liam: any other questions?
[22:22] Marcus: none from me. thanks — good kickoff.
[22:40] Esther: action items recap (see calendar note). I'll add owners/due dates to the crm.
[23:00] Liam: thanks everyone — look forward to the deep dive.
[23:12] (call ends)
---

- Network/security constraints: VPC/private link, customer-managed KMS, SAML/SCIM SSO, SOC2 artifacts required.
- Next steps: SE deep dive week of Aug 10 (proposed Aug 11), runbook and network checklist to be shared by Aug 3.
